author: SW33TS
quote:
Innovative, refreshing, and genuinely a joy to play. When I was younger, I took a sewing class where my teacher told me I was terrible and should never sew again. Little did she know, this game would eventually come along and I'd be creating pieces she'd only dream of making. 

But truly, there's something incredibly charming about the attention to detail and the enjoyment I've found in every piece I've made. Taking my time, trying to get every stitch right, making sure my lines are straight, and seeing everything come together. It's a quiet kind of satisfaction that I've come to appreciate more as I've gotten older.

Sometimes the simplest pleasures make for the most memorable gaming experiences.

author: SW33TS
quote: I really enjoyed the graphical improvements, the smoother and quicker controls, and how much faster some of the enemies felt compared to the original. The added detail in the garments and environments made everything feel more alive, and the expanded abilities of the Ocarina were a fantastic addition. It managed to preserve everything I loved about the original while making meaningful improvements that enhanced the experience. Honestly, everything and more I could have asked for in a remake.
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: SW33TS
quote:
No bandwagon hate here. I went into GTA with an open mind, and my first thought was.  "Why does everything feel SO clunky?" Shooting is stiff, walking feels like I'm trapped in molasses. This isnt how a game  in 2026 should feel esp. after 13 year of development. At times, I genuinely felt like I was playing The Sims, but somehow less fun.

There were some genuinely funny moments, which got a laugh out of me but they seemed so few & far between. 

I think once it releases on PC, RP and private servers will be what really bring this game to life. But for a release title, 30 FPS is insane.

The TV and radio features are cool like always, but beyond that, I'm struggling to see what feels genuinely groundbreaking. 

This is far from a perfect game, and I actually think it might follow a similar trajectory to Cyberpunk. A rocky launch, plenty of criticism, and potentially a much better experience six months down the road.

I'm not writing it off, but I'm certainly not blown away either.
